To change the text size in the Wix Editor: Select the relevant text box in your editor, click Edit Text, optionally highlight specific word(s) you want to resize, then drag the Font size slider to resize the text or enter a specific value between 6 and 999 pixels. If you are using ADI, click the relevant section, click Design, click Customize Section Design, select Text Settings, and drag the Size slider to increase or decrease the font size.

To publish your Wix site and make it live on the internet: 1) Click **Publish** at the top right of the editor (or on the top bar inside ADI). 2) (Optional) Click **View Site** to see your live site. 3) Click **Done** to return to the editor. Note: Clicking Save won't make your changes live—after saving, you must click Publish to show updates on your live site. Once published, your site is available online at your free site URL (siteprefix.wixsite.com/site-name) or connected domain name.

You can edit your published site at any time. Simply open the Editor from your site's dashboard, make the changes you want, and then click Publish again (in the top right of the Editor or top bar of ADI) to make the new changes go live.

Based on the Wix documentation, the third-party POS solutions available for businesses in the UK are Square and SumUp. Wix Mobile POS with Square is available in the UK (along with US, Canada, Japan, Australia, Ireland, and Falkland Islands), allowing you to turn your phone into a point of sale to collect cash or credit card payments. Wix Mobile POS with SumUp is also available in the UK (along with Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Cyprus, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, and Switzerland). Additionally, if Wix Payments POS is not available in your area, Wix notes that these third-party providers (SumUp and Square) can provide solutions for in-person transactions. For inventory synchronization between your POS and eCommerce store, the skuIQ Real-Time Inventory Sync app is available in the UK and integrates with most point-of-sale systems including Clover, Square, Lightspeed, Vend, and Erply.

According to the documentation, the following POS solutions are available in the UK:

1. **Square Mobile POS**: Available in the UK. Setup steps: (1) Download the Wix app from the Apple App Store or Google Play. (2) Download the Square Point of Sale (POS) app to your mobile device. (3) Go to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard and set up Square as your payment provider (note: you need a Premium or Studio plan that supports payments to collect payments). (4) Contact Square to order a free magstripe card reader that plugs into your device's headphone jack.

2. **SumUp Mobile POS**: Available in the UK. Setup steps: (1) Download the Wix app from the App Store or Google Play. (2) Go to Accept Payments in your site's dashboard and connect SumUp as your payment provider (note: you need a Premium or Studio plan that supports payments to collect payments). (3) Contact SumUp to order a Bluetooth card reader that supports swipe, tap, or insert.

3. **Cash Payments**: Available in the UK with no further setup required after downloading the Wix mobile app.

4. **Square POS for Wix Restaurants**: Available in the UK for restaurant sites. Setup steps: (1) Connect Square as your payment provider first. (2) Go to Order Settings in your site's dashboard, click POS Integration, select Square under Point of Sale, and click Add to Site. (3) Enter your Square credentials and select the Square POS location to sync. (4) Set price rounding to "Round half to even" under Order Settings > Advanced > Price Rounding. (5) Activate the Square POS integration toggle under the POS Integration tab.

Being indexed and crawlable is different from ranking high. Google uses many factors beyond keywords—such as site age, backlinks, and searcher location—to determine results placement, so your site may appear on a later page (e.g., 10th, 50th, or 100th) rather than the first page. To improve your ranking: (1) Make sure you've chosen the right keywords by asking what your customers would actually type into Google, and use those keywords naturally throughout your domain, headlines, page text, and image alt text. (2) Generate traffic by regularly publishing fresh, well-written content like blog posts and earning backlinks from relevant or reputable sites to build credibility. (3) Remember that search engines crawl individual pages, not the entire site, so each page is treated separately. (4) Be patient—SEO is a long-term strategy and ranking high takes time and effort, especially in competitive markets; keep adding new pages, images, or blog articles that incorporate your target keywords.

To set up a flat rate shipping fee in Wix Stores (desktop): 1) Go to the Shipping & fulfillment settings in your site's dashboard. 2) Create or select a shipping region (click Add Region to create a new one, or click an existing default rule to edit it). 3) Select 'Flat Rate' from the 'Select how shipping is calculated' drop-down. 4) Enter a name in the Shipping Option Name field (e.g. Standard Shipping). 5) (Optional) Enter an estimated delivery time. 6) Enter the shipping rate. 7) (Optional) Check 'Offer Free Shipping when customer buys over a certain amount' and enter the amount. 8) (Optional) Click 'Add another Delivery Option' for additional options like Express Shipping. 9) (Optional) Check 'Add a handling fee to every order' and enter the fee. 10) Click Save. On the Wix mobile app: Go to Manage > Sales > Orders > Settings icon > Set shipping, tap the region, select Flat Rate from the Shipping method drop-down, tap Next, then create a delivery option by entering a name, optional delivery time, and the rate in the Rate field, then tap Save.

Mobile alignment and overlap issues often occur because different browsers and devices use different rendering engines, causing elements to render differently than in the desktop editor. To resolve overlapping text and elements: open the desktop Editor, break large text blocks into multiple text boxes (one per paragraph), add elements between the text boxes with space between them, and group elements together to ensure alignment. To fix elements appearing in the wrong location on mobile, switch to the mobile editor and manually drag elements to your chosen location; use the Auto Space on Drag tool to create even spacing between elements when placing items in gaps. If elements are missing entirely, check the Hidden on Mobile panel to unhide them. For Pro Gallery specifically, avoid adding separate text or button elements on top of the gallery—use the gallery's built-in Text and Custom Button features instead to prevent alignment issues.

To connect elements on your dynamic item page to CMS collection fields in the Editor: 1) Click the element you want to connect (text, image, or button). 2) Click the Connect to CMS icon. 3) Use the drop-down menus to select the collection field: For text elements, click 'Text connects to' and choose the field to display. For images, use the Connections drop-downs to set 'Image source connects to' (image field), 'Alt text connects to' (Text, Number, Date and Time, Address, or Tags field), 'Tooltip connects to' (same field types), and 'Link connects to' (dataset action, dynamic page, or field). For buttons (Back, Previous, Next), set 'Click action connects to' (dataset action or dynamic page) and optionally 'Label connects to' (field to display on button). Leave elements disconnected if you want content to remain static across all page versions. Click Preview to test each item's version, then Publish when ready.

To prevent an incomplete CMS item from appearing on your live site while using the Wix Editor, enable the Control item visibility feature and set the item's status to Hidden. In the Wix Editor: 1) Click CMS on the left side of the editor, then click Your Collections and select the relevant collection. 2) Click More Actions at the top and select Collection settings. 3) Enable the Control item visibility toggle and choose whether new items should be Visible or Hidden by default (select Hidden to keep new items unpublished until completed), then click Save. 4) To hide a specific item, click the Status field for that item in your collection and select Hidden. Hidden items cannot be read by datasets, so they will not appear on your live site. Changes take effect immediately without needing to publish your site.

If Google's URL Inspection tool says the URL is available to Google and can be indexed but it still isn't appearing in search results, the most common reason is timing: it can take some time for a page to appear, and Google must re-crawl the page before changes or new pages show up in its index. Search engines also cannot guarantee that every page will be indexed, and this is normal in many cases. To help it along, make sure the page is published (search engines can only index published pages and changes made after the last publish won't appear until you publish again), confirm search engines are allowed to index both the page and the site, check that the page has no 301 redirect, reset a customized canonical tag to default, verify there is no 'noindex' robots meta tag, ensure the page is not password protected or members-only, add enough content (at least 250-400 words), and add internal links to the page from other pages on your site. Then use the URL Inspection tool in Google Search Console and click 'Request Indexing' to ask Google to crawl and index the page.

To find the autoplay toggle for a Wix Video player: Go to your editor, click the Wix Video player on your page, click Settings, click the Player tab, and click the 'Autoplay on load' toggle. Enabled means videos play automatically when the page loads (always starting on mute due to browser restrictions); disabled means visitors must click to play. Note: This toggle is not available for strip and slider layouts. For a Single Video Player (such as a Twitch video), the 'Autoplays' toggle is located in the playback options when customizing the video.

To create a website and a new domain with Wix: (1) Sign up for a free Wix account and build your site. (2) To connect a custom domain you must upgrade your site to a Premium plan (selected yearly Premium or Studio plans include a free one-year domain voucher). (3) Purchase the domain directly from Wix: go to Domains in your Wix account, click Get a New Domain, enter a domain name and extension (e.g. .com) and click Search; if available, click Get It, choose the registration period (1–3 years), enter/edit contact information, select a Privacy & Security option (Private Registration and DNSSEC recommended), then select a payment method and submit the purchase. If the domain is unavailable, try another name or extension. Tip: you can use the Wix Business Name Generator to get business name ideas and check suggested domain availability before registering.

To customize the email template for your thank you automation: Go to Automations in your site's dashboard. Create a new automation or edit an existing one. Make sure 'Send an email' is selected as the Action. Click the 'Send an email' action in your flow to open the panel. Under 'Create an email', click Edit to edit your chosen email template. Customize existing elements, add more elements (text, images, videos), and add personalized content (dynamic values). When ready, click Save & Continue/Publish at the top right, then click Activate or Save to activate or save your automation. You can also use More Actions to Preview & test the email or Reset to default template.

A gap below the footer on your live site usually occurs when the content on your page is shorter than the current page length. To resolve it: (1) Change the page background color to match your footer color so the gap looks like part of the footer; (2) Add more content to your page to make it longer and cover most of the viewport (note: a gap may still appear on larger viewports and a scrollbar may appear on smaller ones); (3) Resize the footer to make it longer, which can give the page extra length and cover the viewport; or (4) Check the Layers panel for hidden elements that may be causing the gap and delete or reposition them. If the issue is on a dynamic item page, design according to the shortest item and use strips instead of placing elements freely inside sections.

The Layers icon is located at the bottom of your editor (bottom left). Click it to open the Layers panel, then click Header, Page, or Footer to view the elements in that area. Locate the collapsible text element in the list and click to select it. Once selected, you can manage or adjust the element as needed. If the element is hidden behind another element or outside the gridlines, use the Layers panel to locate and select it directly from the list.

If your PDF update isn't appearing on your live site, you're likely editing the Sandbox collection but haven't synced it to the Live collection (or the Sandbox isn't enabled yet). To resolve this: 1) Enable the Sandbox: Go to CMS in your site's dashboard, click More Actions at the top right, select Advanced Settings, and enable the Sandbox toggle. 2) Sync your changes: Go to your editor, click CMS on the left side, click Your Collections, then click the relevant collection. You should see 'Sandbox Collection' at the top. Select the items you want to sync (or skip selection to sync all), click 'Sync content' at the top right, choose 'Sync all items from Sandbox to Live' (or 'Sync {#} selected items from Sandbox to Live'), and click Sync to confirm. Note that when you sync, updated items in the sandbox overwrite the same items in the live collection, but syncing cannot be undone.

Google Ads with Wix pricing works through a monthly subscription model combined with ad credits and daily spend limits:

**Monthly Subscription**: You pay one monthly amount (billed before VAT) that covers all campaigns you run. This amount is applied directly to your ad credit each month.

**Wix Fee**: Wix takes 15% of your payment for running and optimizing your campaign. The remaining 85% goes toward your ad credit, which is spent on ad clicks.

**Ad Credit**: This is the total money available to run ads across all campaigns. It is spent only on ad link clicks and CTA button clicks using a pay-per-click (PPC) model. Ad credit is paid in USD regardless of the currency you use for your subscription (unless you pay in USD, EUR, GBP, or JPY, in which case credits match that currency).

**Daily Spend**: You set a specific daily amount for each campaign to spend on clicks per day. This is paid up front from your ad credit and is not pay-per-click, though it is optimized to be spent only on ad link clicks and CTA button clicks. Unused daily spend rolls over to the next month's ad credits.

**One-Time Payments**: You can purchase additional ad credits with one-time payments to boost specific campaigns without changing your monthly subscription.

**Promotional Credit**: New Google advertisers can receive a $500 promotional credit (or currency equivalent: 400 EUR, 400 GBP, 60,000 JPY) after spending $500 USD (or equivalent) on ad clicks within the first 60 days of launching. This credit must be spent within 60 days of receiving it and cannot cover subscription renewals.

**Refunds**: All payments (monthly subscriptions and one-time ad credit purchases) are non-refundable.

To allow search engines to index your site: Go to your SEO Dashboard, select 'Go to SEO Settings' under Tools and settings, and make sure the 'Let search engines index your site' toggle is enabled. To submit your sitemap to Google: the easiest way is to complete the Wix SEO Setup Checklist, which connects your site to Google Search Console and automatically submits your sitemap index to Google (note: connecting to Google Search Console requires a Premium plan and a connected domain). Alternatively, you can manually submit your sitemap in Google Search Console by selecting your site, going to Sitemaps, entering 'sitemap.xml' under 'Add a new sitemap', and clicking Submit. You can also submit individual page URLs in Google Search Console by entering the full URL (including https://www) in the search bar and clicking 'Request Indexing'. Keep in mind it can take time for Google to crawl and index your site after these steps.

According to the documentation, to integrate a third-party payment provider you should assign the **Payments Admin** role, which has full access to connect third-party payment providers and manage payment methods.
